name: Moong dal chilla
description: Protein-rich savoury pancakes with pantry-friendly soaked yellow lentils.
instructions: Soak yellow moong dal for 2 hours (or overnight) and blend into a smooth batter with green chilli and ginger.
Mix in finely chopped onions, tomatoes, coriander leaves, and salt.
Heat a tawa with a few drops of oil and spread a ladle of batter thinly.
Cook on medium flame until golden brown on both sides. Serve with mint chutney or curd.

name: Peanut poha
description: A quick, filling breakfast with crunchy roasted peanuts and fresh lemon juice.
instructions: Rinse flattened rice (poha) in a colander until soft, then drain and set aside.
Roast raw peanuts in half a teaspoon of oil until crunchy, then remove.
Splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves in the pan, then saute chopped onions and turmeric.
Gently fold in the softened poha, roasted peanuts, salt, and finish with freshly squeezed lemon juice.

name: Rajma rice bowl
description: A comforting North Indian classic packed with dietary fibre and plant protein.
instructions: Boil soaked red kidney beans (rajma) in a cooker until completely tender.
Saute chopped onions, ginger-garlic paste, tomato puree, and basic masala spices until oil separates.
Add the boiled rajma with cooking broth and simmer on low heat for 12 minutes to thicken the gravy.
Serve warm over steamed basmati or brown rice with sliced onions.

name: Paneer bhurji roti
description: A protein-forward scrambled cottage cheese dish paired with whole-wheat rotis.
instructions: Crumble fresh paneer by hand and keep aside.
Saute chopped onions, green chillies, and tomatoes in a pan with turmeric and garam masala.
Fold in the crumbled paneer and toss on high flame for 3 minutes without drying it out.
Garnish with coriander leaves and pair with 2 warm whole wheat rotis.

name: Chana salad bowl
description: No-fuss raw salad with affordable, filling boiled chickpeas and crisp veggies.
instructions: Rinse boiled or canned white kabuli chana in cold water and place in a mixing bowl.
Dice cucumber, red onion, and tomatoes into bite-sized cubes.
Toss with chaat masala, roasted cumin powder, black salt, and plenty of fresh lime juice.
Enjoy immediately as a refreshing high-fibre midday meal.

name: Egg bhurji with roti
description: Street-style spiced egg scramble loaded with onions and eaten with whole-wheat rotis.
instructions: Whisk 2 fresh eggs with salt and a pinch of turmeric in a small bowl.
Saute finely chopped onions and green chillies in a hot pan until lightly browned.
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes, then pour in the whisked eggs.
Scramble rapidly until cooked through, sprinkle fresh coriander, and enjoy with rotis.

name: Curd rice & cucumber
description: Cooling South Indian comfort dish with probiotics, ideal for hot hostel days.
instructions: Mash soft cooked rice lightly with fresh curd and a splash of milk or water.
Mix in diced cucumber and a pinch of salt.
Prepare a quick tadka: heat 1 tsp oil, splutter mustard seeds, curry leaves, and green chillies.
Pour tadka over the curd rice, stir gently, and serve cool.

name: Soya pulao
description: Ultra budget-friendly plant protein powerhouse cooked in a fragrant one-pot rice meal.
instructions: Soak soya chunks in hot salted water for 15 minutes, drain, and squeeze out all moisture thoroughly.
Heat oil in a pot, add whole spices (cumin, cardamom, bay leaf), sliced onion, and ginger-garlic paste.
Add squeezed soya chunks, green peas, biryani masala, and washed rice; saute for 2 minutes.
Add water, cover with lid, and cook on low flame for 12 minutes until fluffy.

name: Banana curd bowl
description: A quick, energizing sweet snack for the gap between university lectures.
instructions: Whisk cold thick curd in a bowl until smooth.
Slice a ripe banana over the curd.
Top with roasted chia/pumpkin seeds and a drizzle of honey.
Serve cold immediately.

name: Chicken rice plate
description: Lean chicken curry with wholesome rice providing superior amino acids on a budget.
instructions: Marinate boneless chicken pieces with curd, turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt.
Brown sliced onions and ginger-garlic paste in a pan until deeply golden.
Add marinated chicken and simmer with diced tomatoes and seasonal veggies for 18 minutes until tender.
Serve with steamed rice and a wedge of lemon.

name: Boiled eggs & toast
description: Quick hostel staple with two hard-boiled eggs and crisp toasted bread.
instructions: Boil 2 large eggs in salted water for 9 minutes for firm hard-boiled yolks.
Toast 2 slices of whole wheat or multigrain bread until golden.
Peel the eggs, slice in half, season with salt and crushed black pepper.
Serve hot with lightly buttered toast.

name: Dal tadka with jeera rice
description: Aromatic yellow lentil curry tempered with golden cumin and garlic over fragrant rice.
instructions: Pressure-cook yellow toor dal with turmeric and salt until creamy soft.
Cook basmati rice with cumin seeds (jeera) and a pinch of salt.
Make the tadka: heat oil or ghee, splutter cumin, minced garlic, dried red chilli, and diced tomatoes.
Pour sizzing tadka into the dal, swirl, and serve over hot jeera rice.

name: Oats & peanut butter porridge
description: Creamy rolled oats simmered in warm milk, swirled with peanut butter and fruit.
instructions: Boil 1 cup of milk (or water) in a small saucepan.
Add half a cup of rolled oats and cook on low heat for 4 minutes until thick and creamy.
Stir in a heaped tablespoon of peanut butter until melted.
Transfer to a bowl and top with sliced ripe banana.

name: Besan chilla roll
description: Crisp gram-flour crepes loaded with chopped veggies and rolled for on-the-go mornings.
instructions: Whisk gram flour (besan) with water, carom seeds (ajwain), turmeric, and salt into a pourable batter.
Mix in finely minced onions, green chillies, and tomatoes.
Cook on a lightly greased pan for 3 minutes on each side until crisp.
Roll up tightly and serve with green coriander chutney.

name: Palak paneer with roti
description: Iron-rich vibrant spinach gravy cooked with soft cottage cheese cubes.
instructions: Blanch washed spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, then plunge into cold water and blend smooth.
Saute minced garlic, chopped onion, and cumin in oil until fragrant.
Stir in the spinach puree, garam masala, and fresh paneer cubes.
Simmer for 5 minutes and serve with warm rotis.

name: Egg sandwich
description: Double egg toasted sandwich spiced with sliced onions and fresh cracked pepper.
instructions: Make a quick 2-egg spiced omelette with chopped onion and chilli.
Toast 2 slices of whole wheat bread in a pan.
Place the folded omelette and fresh tomato slices between the bread slices.
Cut diagonally and enjoy warm with tea or coffee.

name: Masala khichdi
description: Comforting one-pot lentil and rice porridge cooked with veggies and mild spices.
instructions: Wash equal portions of rice and split yellow moong dal together.
In a cooker, heat oil, add cumin, diced potato, peas, turmeric, and hing.
Add the dal-rice mix with 4 cups of water and salt.
Cook for 3 whistles, stir well, and enjoy with pickle or roasted papad.

name: Roasted peanut chaat
description: Crispy roasted peanuts tossed with onions, tangy lemon, and street spices.
instructions: Take dry roasted salted or plain peanuts in a bowl.
Add finely chopped onion, tomato, and green chilli.
Sprinkle chaat masala, squeeze half a lemon, and toss thoroughly.
Garnish with chopped coriander for an instant hostel study snack.

name: Aloo paratha with curd
description: Spiced mashed potato stuffed flatbread served with fresh cooling curd.
instructions: Boil, peel, and mash 1 potato with chopped coriander, green chilli, amchur, and salt.
Roll out a portion of whole wheat dough, place the potato filling inside, seal, and roll flat.
Cook on a medium hot tawa with a little ghee or oil until crisp and brown on both sides.
Serve with a cup of chilled fresh curd.

name: Chicken egg fried rice
description: High-protein student dinner combining chicken cubes, scrambled egg, and rice.
instructions: In a wok, scramble 1 egg with salt, then remove and set aside.
Stir-fry seasoned diced chicken pieces on high heat for 6 minutes until cooked.
Add sliced onions, peas, cooked cold rice, soy sauce, and black pepper.
Toss in the scrambled egg, mix on high heat for 2 minutes, and serve.

name: Sprouts chaat bowl
description: Live sprouted green gram packed with active enzymes, vitamins, and protein.
instructions: Steam or lightly microwave sprouted green moong for 2 minutes (or use fresh raw).
Combine with diced cucumber, tomato, and fresh mint or coriander leaves.
Season with roasted cumin powder, black salt, and freshly squeezed lemon juice.
Toss and enjoy crisp, refreshing nutrition.

name: Soya bhurji roti
description: High-protein vegan minced soya scramble cooked with spices and eaten with rotis.
instructions: Soak soya granules or crushed chunks in boiling hot water for 10 minutes, squeeze dry.
Saute cumin seeds, chopped onions, ginger, and green chilli in 1 tsp oil.
Add chopped tomatoes and spices, then fold in the squeezed soya granules.
Cook for 6 minutes on medium heat, garnish with coriander, and serve with 2 rotis.

name: Egg curry with rice
description: Two golden-fried boiled eggs simmered in a flavourful onion-tomato gravy.
instructions: Hard-boil 2 eggs, peel, poke lightly with a fork, and shallow fry in turmeric-oil until golden.
In the same pan, saute minced onion, ginger-garlic paste, and tomato puree until thick.
Add coriander powder, garam masala, salt, and half a cup of water.
Drop in the eggs, simmer for 5 minutes, and serve with steamed rice.

name: Seasonal fruit & roasted seeds
description: Fresh sliced local seasonal fruit (apple, guava, papaya) topped with roasted seeds.
instructions: Wash and slice fresh seasonal fruit of your choice.
Sprinkle a tablespoon of mixed roasted sunflower or pumpkin seeds.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice and a dash of chaat masala if desired.
